Subject: RE: FW: Novaterra MSA redlines - IP / indemnity

Jonas — quick read and initial take. I annotated their redline and included a short playbook we can propose. See attached (km_comments_redline.docx). Highlights / suggested positions:

1) Defense control: we should keep primary defense control. Offer a limited customer-control carveout only when:
   - the claim relates solely to Customer-supplied material (Customer Data, Customer Models) and
   - the claim would not require Redwood to materially change the runtime (i.e., the claim is about Customer content).
   - If we grant this, require Customer to bear incremental defense costs above a baseline and to reimburse Redwood for settlement amounts that meet a reasonableness threshold.

2) Scope: tighten "Customer IP" definition so it excludes standard OSS dependencies and third-party models that are subject to their own upstream licenses. Put burden on Customer to provide evidence linking the claim to Customer Content.

3) Cap and offsets: accept an order-form cap (we propose tying cap to 12 months of ARR for the order form) but push back on full insurance-offset that allows Customer to reduce our cap by the full policy limit. Propose insurance-offset only for third-party claims where Customer can show an actual recovery; otherwise no automatic offset.

4) Cooperation / evidence: add an explicit evidence-handling timeline: Customer must produce evidence within 10 business days of notice; if not produced, Redwood can assume defense control and suspend related services.

5) SLA for notice: require Customer to give prompt notice and support our subpoena/submission requests; allow Redwood to deny coverage if notice is materially delayed and Redwood is prejudiced.

I'll draft a 1-page "playbook" summarizing these concessions and open asks so Sales can present this in the next customer call. Ben — can your CS/Tech Ops team confirm the practical timeline for evidence handoff (we suggested 10 business days above)? Also share who on your side would own evidence collection.

From: Michael Chen <michael.chen@novaterra.com>

Subject: RE: Novaterra MSA redlines - IP / indemnity

Jonas / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side and where we are unlikely to move: 

- Customer control: Novaterra cannot accept Redwood having unilateral defense control for claims that arise from our customers' use of the joint solution when the alleged infringement is rooted in the product functionality we purchase from Redwood. For business continuity and reputational reasons, our legal and product teams must be able to control the response where the claim is about our processing of customer data or our use of specific model features.

- Insurance offset: we proposed insurance offset because our board requires us to maintain a practical loss-mitigation path. We're open to language that prevents duplicative recoveries, but an automatic prohibition on offsets would make it impossible for us to sign.

- Evidence: we can commit to producing reasonable evidence, but our product team needs time to triage (usually 7-12 business days depending on the ingestion pipeline). The 10-business-day window is tight for complex outputs that require replays.

I've attached our annotated comments where we flagged the defense-control carve and the proposed cap increase. We would like to schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to work through the defense-control draft language rather than iterate by email.
